title: Catastrophic Medical Hardship Adjustment: Liability Cap Percent and Lookback Months Across the Patient Financial Assistance Program
content:
Two figures of the Patient Financial Assistance Program apply only to the Catastrophic Medical Hardship Adjustment: the percent of annual household income above which the patient's laboratory responsibility is forgiven, and the number of calendar months before the application date over which that laboratory responsibility is totalled.

| Tier | Liability cap, percent of annual household income | Months of laboratory responsibility totalled before the application date |
|---|---|---|
| Financial Assistance 25% Discount | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (not applicable) |
| Financial Assistance 50% Discount | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (not applicable) |
| Financial Assistance 75% Discount | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (not applicable) |
| Financial Assistance Full Discount | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (not applicable) |
| Presumptive Eligibility Full Discount | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (not applicable) |
| Catastrophic Medical Hardship Adjustment | 10 | 12 |

## Notes on the two figures

- **Liability cap.** For the Catastrophic Medical Hardship Adjustment the cap is 10 percent of annual household income. The part of the patient's laboratory responsibility above that amount is what the hardship tier forgives.
- **Lookback.** The laboratory responsibility compared with the cap is totalled over dates of service in the 12 calendar months before the application date, the application date included.
- A figure of 0 in this schedule means the figure does not apply to that tier.

**Illustration (hypothetical household).** Annual household income of $38000.00 gives a liability cap of $3800.00, which is 10 percent of that income.
